title: India’s Russian oil dilemma
dek: India promised Washington it would stop buying Russian oil. Then war closed the Gulf. Now the Gulf is back on top and the US tariff threat is on hold.
bigLabel: India's crude imports so far in November: Persian Gulf vs Russia, per Kpler

glance.what: Russian crude filled the gap when Hormuz was disrupted. In October the US waived its threatened tariffs on big buyers of Russian oil, and in November India's imports from the Gulf overtook Russia's for the first time since the Iran war began.
glance.why: Cheap Russian oil cushions India's import bill; being punished for it would raise costs and strain relations with the US.
glance.next: The waiver is temporary. Whether Russian crude stays competitive as Gulf supplies recover.

forYou: This story decides how much India pays for oil and how exposed exporters are to US penalties.
next: Whether the US restores the tariff threat, and how much Russian crude India keeps buying.

events.title: India agrees to halt Russian oil under the US deal
events.summary: The commitment is part of the package that was meant to cut US tariffs to 18%.

events.title: Hormuz shuts; analysts expect a return to Russian oil
events.summary: Nomura says India may secure Russian oil via eastern routes and buy more from the US, West Africa and Latin America.

events.title: Russian crude imports reach a reported record
events.summary: India’s Russian crude intake is reported at a record 2.25 million barrels a day, and about 70% of its crude now avoids Hormuz.

events.title: US law names India at risk of tariffs up to 100%
events.summary: The new sanctions law targets the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas.

events.title: Trump waives the Russian-oil tariffs
events.summary: An executive order waives the sanctions and duties of up to 100% that the new US law allowed on the biggest buyers of Russian oil. The waiver is not specific to India and could be reversed.

events.title: Gulf overtakes Russia for the first time since the war
events.summary: India's crude imports from the Persian Gulf reach about 2.1 million barrels a day so far in November, above Russia's 1.8 million, as Hormuz flows recover and Russian oil loses its price edge on higher freight costs.
